name: Horde
strategy: Use large formations, overlapping engagements, and numerical superiority.
qualificationNote: A formation containing four or more surviving Models qualifies for the standard numerical requirements of this doctrine.

commands.name: Endless Ranks
commands.effect: One friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models counts as one additional Unit for objective control until the end of the Round.

commands.name: Massed Volley
commands.effect: One friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models gains +2 Attacks on its next ranged Attack this Phase. If another friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models is within Short, gain +3 Attacks instead.

commands.name: Mob Tactics
commands.effect: One friendly Unit gains +2 Attacks on its next Engagement Attack against an enemy also Engaged by a different friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models.

commands.name: Pack Coordination
commands.effect: When a friendly Unit within Short of another friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models is attacked, it gains Tough 2 against that Attack.

commands.name: Encirclement
commands.effect: One friendly Unit attacking an enemy also Engaged by a different friendly Unit with at least four surviving Models causes that enemy to worsen Evade by one step against the Attack.

doctrineIdentity: Numerical advantage and coordinated formations. Standard generic Line Infantry and Ranged Infantry qualify without reinforcement. Larger hordes remain more reliable because they retain their model-count requirements after suffering casualties.
